transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: Stop there. The stone you're standing on is safer than the ones around it.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: You’ve been watching me since I arrived.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: Watching keeps a man alive longer than courage does down here.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: Then watch closely. I'm looking for someone.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: Lower your voice before the houses decide they want to listen.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I’m not afraid of the houses.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: You will be once they start remembering you.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: My brother Omar fell into this place. A pale hand dragged him down.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: Then the well noticed him. That rarely ends well.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: You're the first living person I've seen here. That makes you useful.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: Careful with that word. People who treat this place like a problem to solve usually disappear first.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: How long have you been standing beside this fountain?

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: Long enough that the sky became something I remember instead of something I see.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: And yet you're still breathing.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: Breathing is easy. Staying yourself is harder.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: What takes people first?

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: Names. Faces. Then the reasons you came here.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: Then I’ll keep Omar’s name where it belongs.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: Good. Don't throw it into the air. The dark likes collecting names.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: What are the things in those houses?

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: Jinn. Old watchers who enjoy seeing how long visitors last.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: And the oil?

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: Don't touch it. It doesn't burn your skin. It marks your mind.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I noticed the bubbling changed when I spoke earlier.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: Fear and noise both stir it.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: You said some people made it out.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: A few crawled away breathing. None of them left whole.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: Then survival is possible.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: Possible and expensive.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I’m willing to pay.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: Everyone says that before the dark starts collecting.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: You survived by standing here. What did you hold onto when the fear got loud?

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: Something simple.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: A thought? A word?

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: A sentence.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: Then give it to me.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: You think words are tools. Down here they are bait.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I’m not leaving without something that helps me keep my head.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: If I give it to you, the square will notice. It already takes memories when I help strangers.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: You're already helping by talking.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: Talking costs less than giving.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: My brother is down there because of me.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: Guilt makes people brave. It also makes them careless.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: Then consider me both.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: No.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: No?

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: I will not give you the words.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: Even knowing what I'm walking into?

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: Yes.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: Why?

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: Because the last man I helped forgot his own name before he reached the stairs.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: And you think silence is kinder.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: Sometimes survival means learning the hard way.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: Then I’ll learn.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: Maybe you will.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: If I make it back, I’ll ask you again.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: If you make it back, you may not remember what you meant to ask.
